title: Word Search II
hints: searching for each word independently repeats a lot of the same board exploration - could the words share a search structure?
insert every candidate word into a trie, marking end-of-word nodes
run one DFS per starting cell, but walk the trie alongside the board: only continue into a neighbor if the trie has a child edge for that neighbor's letter
when a trie node marked end-of-word is reached, record that word as found - but keep exploring, since one word can be a prefix of another
mark cells visited going down and unmark them coming back up, exactly like single-word word search, so the same cell can be reused by other paths
commonMistakes: reusing a cell within the same word's trace (must track per-trace visited cells and undo on backtrack)
producing output words out of alphabetical or trie-discovery order instead of preserving the original input word list order
stopping the DFS as soon as a word is found instead of continuing, which misses other words that share that word as a prefix
not handling a candidate word that is longer than the total cell count as an automatic miss before searching

content.problemStatement:
You're given a grid of lowercase letters, encoded as a string where each row is a run of letters and rows are separated by "|". For example, `"oaan|etae|ihkr|iflv"` is this 4x4 grid:

```
o a a n
e t a e
i h k r
i f l v
```

You're also given a space-delimited list of candidate `words`. For each candidate word, it can be traced out by moving from cell to cell in the grid, where each step must move to a horizontally or vertically adjacent cell, and no cell may be reused within a single word's trace. A fresh trace, with all cells available again, is allowed for each new word.

**Return the candidate words that can be found, space-delimited, in the same order they appeared in the input word list.**
constraints: 1 <= rows, cols <= 6 for the decoded board
the board and all words consist of lowercase English letters only
notes: a candidate word longer than the total number of cells in the board (always not found)
two different candidate words that share a long common prefix
a word whose letters all exist in the board, but never in a connected adjacent path
the same letter repeated densely across the board, forcing real backtracking

sampleTestCases.explanation: oath traces (0,0)o -> (0,1)a -> (1,1)t -> (2,1)h; eat traces (1,3)e -> (1,2)a -> (1,1)t; pea and rain cannot be traced
(0,0) and (1,1) are diagonal, not adjacent, so "ad" cannot be traced
"yz" would need y at (0,1) adjacent to z, but z is at (1,0), a diagonal, so it fails

optimal.time: O(rows * cols * 4^L) total, shared across all words instead of paying the search cost once per word
optimal.space: O(total characters across all words) for the trie, plus O(L) recursion depth
optimal.pattern: build a trie of all candidate words once, then run a single combined backtracking DFS from every board cell, following trie edges so failing prefixes are abandoned across all words at once

bruteForce.approach: for each word, independently DFS from every cell in the board, exploring all four directions with no pruning across different words, checking each full path against the word
bruteForce.time: O(W * rows * cols * 4^L) where W is the number of words and L is the max word length
